children: Chicago wheat futures rallied for a fourth session on Wednesday, supported by disruption to the Black Sea grain trade.
Soybean rose and snapped two sessions of losses while market players awaited developments from US President Donald Trump's meeting with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later this week. Corn inched higher.
The most-traded wheat contract on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT)
added 0.04% at $6.10-1/2 a bushel at 0107GMT. Soybean
gained 0.31% at $12.29-1/4 a bushel and CBOT corn

Ukrainian drones and missiles on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the Crimea bridge, which used by commercial vessels entering and leaving the Sea of Azov, making it an important part of the region's grain export network

Ukraine's grain harvest could halve to 30 million metric tons next year from 62 million tons in 2026 if farmers scale back plantings because they are unable to export the crop, agriculture minister Taras Vysotskiy told Reuters on Tuesday.
Soybeans continued to flood into the US Midwest supply chain as farmers wrap up their fall harvest, with farmers expected to harvest their largest crop ever this autumn.

The lowest price offered in the tender from South Korean importer Cargill Agri Purina (CAPI) on Tuesday to buy up to 70,000 metric tons of animal feed corn was estimated at $265.49 a ton cost and freight included (c&f), traders said.
President Donald Trump will meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping later this week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' summit in China.
Stocks fell across the globe on Tuesday, weighed down by tech shares, while Nvidia results after the bell lifted US equity futures and a tech-heavy Korean ETF.
